meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common feminine noun meaning 'jacket, coat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На улице холодно, возьми тёплую куртку.
examples.trans: It's cold outside, take a warm jacket.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, go on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go on, tell me: how much is here?

снимать.gloss: to take off; to film; to rent

meanings.en: to take off; to film; to rent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take off; to film; to rent', paired with 'снять'.

examples.trans: Watch. I'm taking off my ring.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'рюга'). Common Russian noun meaning 'crook, big thief' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You look like some rich crook.
Which one of us is a crook?

examples.text: Не верю. Похож на какого-то богатого ворюгу.
examples.trans: I don't buy it. You look like some rich crook.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.
Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stop, quit', paired with 'прекращать'.

examples.trans: Stop it! We will have the flat.

examples.text: Да ну что вы, прекратите! Это жизнь.
examples.trans: Oh, come on, stop it! That's life.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

заболеть.gloss: to fall ill, to get sick

meanings.en: to fall ill, to get sick
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'болеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall ill, to get sick', paired with 'болеть'.

examples.text: Вчера он заболел и остался дома.
examples.trans: Yesterday he fell ill and stayed at home.

examples.text: А у меня учительница по математике заболела.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'лица'). Common feminine noun meaning 'street; outside' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are reporters out on the street!

examples.text: Там на улице журналисты! Они меня ждут!
examples.trans: There are reporters out on the street! They're waiting for me!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Подожди, там же в марте холодно!
examples.trans: Hold on, it's cold there in March!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трашный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('terrible, scary').

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'viral cold, flu' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Just an ordinary viral cold, nothing too terrible.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая инфекция.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new viral cold.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sick, ill; (as a noun) patient').

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I don't know whether he is at home.
Was it Osipenko who hired you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'medic, doctor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый медик.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new medic.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'носить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bring', paired with 'принести'.

examples.text: Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.

examples.text: И не надо больше никаких документов сюда приносить!
examples.trans: And don't bring any more documents in here!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('warm').

examples.trans: And where are your warm gloves?

examples.text: Да, его тёплая шапка лежит прямо здесь.
examples.trans: Yes, his warm hat is lying right here.

examples.text: Снимайте скорее с него тёплые валенки.
examples.trans: Take off his warm felt boots quickly.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean'.

examples.trans: Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'along; by; about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мойка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'dumpster, trash heap, rubbish dump' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Take the bag to the trash dump.

examples.text: Ладно, я отнесу её на помойку.
examples.trans: Okay, I will take it to the dumpster.
He found a box in the dumpster.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to climb, snoop around'.

examples.text: Значит, может мне тоже по помойкам лазить?
examples.trans: So maybe I should go climbing around the dumpsters too?

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет лазить без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to climb without a reason.
